trajectory.title: The witness layer
trajectory.description: 15 real nervous-system wirings — mapped from actual organisms by electron microscopy — answer deterministic tasks, and every answer carries a receipt anyone can replay. Compute run over nature's wiring: the first living-cloud service.

trajectory.title: The sensing commons
trajectory.description: EcoCell One listeners near forests, reefs and farms — quorum-witnessed readings, guardian custody, per-contribution credit. Fully built and e2e-tested; the field-validation gate (E0) is what remains.

trajectory.title: Compute by living systems
trajectory.description: Hyper-efficient compute done by nature itself. The organism-compute lane graduates only when an evidence fingerprint lands — the preserved-wiring leg already passes (15/15 relays replay bit-for-bit); the living half stays refused until it earns it.

trajectory.title: Storage inside living systems
trajectory.description: Data embedded in DNA by non-invasive methods not yet known. The density is field-proven — 215 petabytes per gram; the read/write interface is the open problem, and it enters only with consent.

thesis: The thesis: biology already beats silicon on energy per synapse (~1–100 pJ) and storage density (215 PB/g). Whether the other axes follow is the question this project exists to answer — every step ships a receipt.

axes.today: simulation on silicon; organism compute refused
axes.field: biological synapse ~1–100 pJ/event vs TrueNorth ~26 pJ (Science 2014) and Loihi ~23.6 pJ (IEEE Micro 2018)

axes.today: biological dynamics slower than GHz silicon — reported, not hidden
axes.field: no published evidence supports a win here
biological parallelism exists (a brain runs ~86B neurons on ~20 W) but mapping it to useful throughput is unproven

axes.today: the evidence ledger — receipts, not bulk data
axes.field: DNA reaches 215 PB/g (Erlich, Science 2017) vs conventional media; the non-invasive read/write interface is unknown — and enters only with consent
